rss.title: 62,077 Raindrops vs. One Window – Watch the Last Dry Spot Vanish #simulation #rain #asmr
rss.desc:
Rain on a window at night -- watch every drop land, merge and run until the very last dry spot is gone. Where do you think it will be?

Every raindrop is simulated: when two drops touch, they become one and keep all of their water -- so two equal drops make one that is only 26 % wider. A drop clings to the glass until its weight beats its grip, then it suddenly runs and sweeps up everything below it. And look closely: every single drop is a tiny lens and shows the city upside down.

Make sure to select the 4K quality setting to see the city in every drop!

What you'll find in this video:
0:00 - A Dry Window
1:25 - Half the Glass Is Wet
2:45 - 10 % Left
3:29 - The Last Percent
4:00 - The Last Dry Spot
4:21 - Wet

Tell me in the comments: did you guess where the last dry spot would be?

Everything you see and hear was simulated and rendered with my own code -- every drop, every reflection and every sound. Even the rain you hear comes from the simulation: every drop that hits the glass makes its own soft tap, and each chime is a drop landing, merging or starting to run.

Don't forget to Like and Subscribe if you want to see more satisfying simulations!

rss.title: Reactor Meltdown | Six Shapes, Six Voices
rss.desc:
Twelve balls move through six distinct chambers: a circle, triangle, square, pentagon, hexagon and star. Each shape has its own synthesized voice, with actual collisions triggering the notes. Wall breaks and ball transfers build toward a shared reactor finale.

THE SIMULATION
The renderer and collision system share the six chamber contours. Every breakable wall and core shell has 96 hit points. Twelve conserved balls end as six chamber keepers and six core captures; the last capture starts the reactor ignition. This is a designed arcade-style model.

HOW IT WAS MADE
Custom Python simulation and rendering produce native 4K images. Each chamber has its own synthesized voice and pitch family: warm wood, glass, soft metal, plucked string, low marimba and shimmering bell. Actual impacts trigger notes, with a shared rate cap to keep the mix controlled.

Created for Satisfying Physics Simulation with AI-assisted code development.

rss.title: The Most Satisfying Polyrhythm Engine
rss.desc:
What happens when 32 concentric regular polygons — from an inner 3-sided triangle all the way to an outer 34-sided polygon — orbit at exact integer harmonic ratios? 

At first, the glowing travelers appear to drift into complex geometric chaos. Yet because their orbital frequencies follow exact Diophantine ratios f_k = (C + k) / T, the entire system spontaneously snaps into breathtaking star symmetries at rational fractions of the Grand Cycle (1/6, 1/4, 1/3, 1/2, 2/3, and 3/4) before reuniting in a 100% Grand Phase-Lock at 12 o'clock!

Every single note you hear is synthesized directly from the geometry in real time (48 kHz Stereo): whenever an orb bounces off a polygon vertex, it triggers a warm Rosewood Marimba and Crystal Harp tone in D-Dorian / F-Lydian, stereo-panned to the exact horizontal position of the vertex.

🎧 Put on headphones, set the quality to 4K 60FPS, and watch pure number theory turn into music.

⏱️ CHAPTERS:
0:00 Act I: The Sacred Triad (Triangle, Square & Pentagon — 3:4:5 Spirograph Web)
0:44 Act II: The Octave of Polygons (8 Nested Polygons — 3-gon to 10-gon)
1:32 Act III: The 16-Chamber Resonator (16 Polygons — Quadrant & Triskelion Star Locks)
2:22 Act IV: The 32-Body Grand Alignment (32 Polygons — 3-gon to 34-gon)
3:08 Finale: 100% Grand Phase-Lock Convergence at 12 O'Clock

🔬 SIMULATION & AUDIO TELEMETRY:
• Geometry Engine: Exact Parametric N-Gon Perimeter Solver (Python / NumPy / OpenCV)
• Polygon Range: 3-gon (Triangle) up to 34-gon
• Orbital Law: Diophantine Frequency Ratios f_k = (C_base + k) / T_cycle
• Symmetry Resonances: 1:6 Hexagonal, 1:4 Quadrant Cross, 1:3 Triskelion Triad, 1:2 Bipolar Axis & 1:1 Apex Lock
• Audio Synthesis: 48 kHz Stereo Rosewood Marimba + Crystal Harp Overtone Synthesizer & Ambient Harmonic Pad
• Resolution: 3840x2160 (4K UHD) @ 60 FPS
• Random Numbers Used: 0 (100% Deterministic Number Theory)
